messages.subject: rebalancing the data
messages.body_plain:
suppose that I have a binary target with 5% ones and 95% zeroes, and I
wish to apply neural nets.  I might want to train on a dataset that
has, say, 50% ones and 50% zeroes.  Is there an easy way to create
such a dataset in Rattle, or do I have to do it in R?  (I know how to
do it in R, I am just wondering whether it can be done in Rattle.)

Regards,

Bruce

messages.subject: Re: rebalancing the data
messages.body_plain:
Hi Bruce,

Not supported in Rattle just yet but it would be a useful option.

Perhaps a "Balanced" check button on the Data tab before the "Seed:"
option? What R code do you use to do this (and what options to the
balancing do you employ)?

Not quite sure how it would work in the context of Partition. Perhaps,
if we are replicating the "ones" then we can ensure each partition is
also balanced?

Regards,
Graham

messages.subject: suggestion for Data tab
messages.body_plain:
I have 300 variables in my dataset.  I don't want to have to click
"ignore" 280 times when I want to create a 20 variable model.  There
should be a button at the top so that I can click on it and all the
variables get set to "ignore".  Then I can just change 20 of them to
"input".

messages.subject: Re: suggestion for Data tab
messages.body_plain:
On 13 March 2011 15:22, B D McCullough <bdmccu...@drexel.edu> wrote:
> I have 300 variables in my dataset.  I don't want to have to click
> "ignore" 280 times when I want to create a 20 variable model.  There
> should be a button at the top so that I can click on it and all the
> variables get set to "ignore".  Then I can just change 20 of them to
> "input".

Already there...

In the window showing the list of variables, type Ctrl-A (to select
all variables) or else manually select variables groups at a time with
Ctrl and Shift with the mouse button. Once all are highlighted that
you wish to Ignore then click the Ignore button just above the list of
variables.

Regards,
Graham
